EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The past 24 hours have been dominated by contradictory reports of Iranian missile strikes targeting US bases in Jordan, with Iran confirming the attacks and US officials denying knowledge. Concurrently, Israel announced the complete capture of the strategic Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, a significant blow to Hezbollah, with reports indicating 70-100 Hezbollah and IRGC Quds Force members trapped in tunnels.

IRAN
Iran's Army Spokesperson Brigadier General Akrami Nia stated that the recent military operations against US bases were "rapid," "devastating," and "widespread," targeting US bases from Jordan to the UAE using "Fath missiles" and "Arash 2 drones" equipped with AI. However, a senior US official denied any attacks on US bases in Jordan, while Al Arabiya reported that missiles targeting Jordan were intercepted. Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi challenged Jordan's account of Iran's response, asking how long Iran should wait to respond to aggression that used Arab airspace and territory and reiterating that Iranian defensive strikes targeted US military facilities, not civilian areas, a claim Qatar reportedly affirmed in a document to the ITU.

Economically, the US Treasury Department sanctioned Golden Global Bank in Turkey and two affiliated companies for facilitating millions of dollars in transactions for the IRGC Quds Force and providing access to the international banking network. US Treasury Secretary Scott Basnet claimed the EU has officially joined the "economic expulsion" campaign against Iran and stated that no Iranian crude oil has successfully passed through the Strait of Hormuz to China since the US blockade was reimposed. He projected oil prices could fall to $40-50 per barrel after the current situation. Vice President J.D. Vance asserted US control over the Strait of Hormuz, claiming 15 million barrels were extracted yesterday. Oman reportedly rejected Iran's proposal for shared fees for passage through the strait.

Internally, President Raisi emphasized national unity to counter enemy plots aimed at creating division. Iran's Judiciary Chief Gholam-Hossein Mohseni Eje'i met with the Chief Justice of India and the President of China’s Supreme People’s Court to expand judicial cooperation. IRGC Intelligence arrested a seven-member cell linked to anti-Iran Kurdish separatist groups, seizing firearms and ammunition in western Iran. Press TV reported 767 US troops wounded in the "war with Iran," a figure not corroborated by other sources.

ISRAEL
Israeli forces conducted several military operations in the past 24 hours. The IDF announced the elimination of Mohammad Mahmoud Marshad al-Qadi, a Hamas Nukhba company commander, in Khan Younis. Al-Qadi was responsible for leading the October 7 raid on the Sufa army post and for holding hostages in the Rafah area, and was reportedly involved in rebuilding Hamas capabilities in violation of the ceasefire.

In the West Bank, Duvdevan Commando Unit soldiers, acting on Shin Bet intelligence, arrested five individuals in Qabatiya suspected of planning a terror attack, seizing an M16 assault rifle and other military gear from their homes. In the Shomron region, a 48-hour operation led to the destruction of over 30 lathes used for manufacturing weapons, the confiscation of hidden weapons, and the arrest of more than 10 wanted individuals. In Jerusalem, Border Police neutralized an assailant attempting a stabbing attack near the Damascus Gate; no Israeli casualties were reported.

On the home front, a fire broke out near the settlement of Gevaot in Gush Etzion, leading to the evacuation of the first line of houses, with fire fighting aircraft and ground crews working to contain it. Politically, Gilad Erdan withdrew "The Unity Party" from the upcoming elections after failing to secure enough support or an alliance with Benny Gantz's "Blue and White" party. Tali Gottlieb will be number 2 on Itamar Ben Gvir's "Otzma Yehudit" party list. An Israeli civilian was indicted for "security offenses" after being operated by foreign intelligence elements in a "foreign influence" campaign against Israel.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces carried out large-scale demolitions and an intentional explosion in the Bani Suheila area, east of Khan Younis, in the southern Gaza Strip. In northern Gaza, forces operating east of the Yellow Line came under fire, to which the IDF responded by striking the area, emphasizing this was a "blatant violation of the ceasefire agreement." The IDF confirmed the elimination of Hamas commander Mohammad Mahmoud Marshad al-Qadi in Khan Younis, citing his role in the October 7 attacks and recent efforts to rebuild Hamas capabilities.

LEBANON
Israel's Defense Minister Israel Katz announced the "completion of control" over the strategic Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, stating that IDF forces had "cleared Hezbollah's command and control tunnels," which served as the last defensive outpost for the Nabatiyeh area. An IRGC official reported to the New York Times that between 70 and 100 Hezbollah members, including Iranian Quds Force advisors, have been trapped in tunnels around Ali al-Taher since June, with Israeli forces reportedly targeting those attempting to retrieve supplies.

Israeli artillery strikes were reported in Zawtar Al-Sharqiyeh and Al-Mansouri in southern Lebanon. Press TV reported Israeli forces detonating civilian homes in Bani Hayyan and a drone strike targeting a motorcycle near Kafr Roummane. The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) facilitated the return of five detainees from Israeli custody to Lebanon: two Lebanese citizens (Ali Shour and Hussein Ayash) and two Syrian citizens (Assad al-Hasika and Wissam al-Samawy), in addition to one person returned yesterday.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Syria has begun the destruction of remnants from its secret chemical weapons program, first identified in May, with the UN confirming this is the first verifiable destruction of chemical weapons since 2014.

In Iraq, the Oil Ministry announced that crude oil exports in August reached nearly 70 million barrels, marking the highest level since the war began in the region. However, Baghdad and several other provinces are experiencing a severe fuel crisis, with long queues at gas stations due to a daily deficit of approximately 5 million liters between gasoline production and consumption. Reports indicate that the Turkish intelligence service will oversee the PKK's disarmament and withdrawal from 72 locations in Iraq, with five arms handover points established on the Erbil-Sulaymaniyah border. ISIS has claimed responsibility for an attack on a Popular Mobilization Forces vehicle in the Anbar desert.

GULF STATES
The UAE President, Mohammed bin Zayed, engaged in discussions with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan concerning regional developments and bilateral cooperation. Reports from the Wall Street Journal, cited by Kian Meli 1, indicate that Dubai and other Gulf states are experiencing a severe decline in tourism, flights, hotel occupancy (down to 56%), and real estate sales (luxury sales down 59%) due to the "US-Iran war." Saudi oil exports have reportedly slumped to a nine-year low, attributed to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the Yemeni blockade, according to Press TV.

The US has deployed 12 F-16 fighter jets and KC-46A refueling aircraft to Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia. Qatar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs asserted that Qatar is not a party to the conflict and that attacks on its civilian territory and infrastructure are "unjustifiable" and a "clear violation of international law." This statement came after Iran claimed Qatar admitted that Iranian defensive strikes only hit US military facilities on Qatari soil, not civilian targets.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Contradictory Reports on Iranian Missile Strikes**: Iranian sources, including Army Spokesperson Akrami Nia, claimed widespread missile and drone attacks on US bases from Jordan to the UAE. US officials, however, denied knowledge of any attacks on their bases in Jordan.
2.  **Capture of Ali al-Taher Ridge**: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz declared the full capture of the strategic Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, reporting the clearance of Hezbollah command and control tunnels and destruction of infrastructure. An IRGC official confirmed 70-100 Hezbollah and IRGC Quds Force members trapped in tunnels in the area since June.
3.  **Hamas Commander Elimination**: The IDF and Shin Bet killed Mohammad Mahmoud Marshad al-Qadi, a Hamas Nukhba company commander, in Khan Younis, citing his role in the Oct 7 Sufa post raid and hostage-holding, and his recent efforts to rebuild Hamas capabilities.
4.  **US-EU Push for Iran Nuclear Referral to UNSC**: The US, France, UK, and Germany are working to pass an IAEA resolution next week to report Iran to the UN Security Council for non-compliance with the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.
5.  **US Economic Sanctions on Iran**: The US Treasury sanctioned a Turkish bank (Golden Global Bank) and two affiliates for facilitating transactions for the IRGC Quds Force, claiming the EU has also officially joined the "economic expulsion" campaign against Iran.
6.  **Strait of Hormuz Standoff**: US Vice President J.D. Vance asserted that 15 million barrels of oil were extracted from the Strait of Hormuz yesterday under US control, while Oman reportedly rejected an Iranian proposal for shared fees for passage.
7.  **Arrest of Terror Plotters in West Bank**: IDF Duvdevan commandos arrested five individuals in Qabatiya, West Bank, suspected of planning a terror attack, seizing an M16 rifle and other weapons.
8.  **Chemical Weapons Destruction in Syria**: The UN confirmed that Syria has begun destroying remnants of its secret chemical weapons program identified in May, marking the first verifiable destruction of such weapons since 2014.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The situation remains highly volatile with significant escalation risks. The reported Iranian missile strikes on US bases, even with US denials of impact, indicate a direct and kinetic engagement that could quickly escalate if confirmed to have caused damage or casualties. The decisive Israeli capture of the Ali al-Taher ridge represents a major blow to Hezbollah's operational capabilities in southern Lebanon and may provoke a strong retaliatory response from Hezbollah or Iran. The trapping of IRGC Quds Force advisors in the tunnels further heightens the risk of direct Iranian involvement if attempts to rescue them fail.

The push by Western powers to refer Iran's nuclear file to the UN Security Council could significantly raise diplomatic pressure and potentially lead to further sanctions, which Iran has previously responded to with escalatory nuclear activities. Economic pressures, including new US sanctions on financial entities in Turkey and claims of an effective US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, are active flashpoints. Iran's military rhetoric asserting sovereignty over Hormuz and threats of pre-emptive operations indicate red lines that could trigger wider conflict if challenged. The ongoing "hybrid attacks" in Germany and the general instability impacting Gulf states' economies signal a broadening scope of indirect conflict.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States**: Vice President J.D. Vance stated the US will not engage in talks with Iran until they cease firing on commercial shipping, claiming the US extracted 15 million barrels from the Strait of Hormuz yesterday and emphasizing US ability to guarantee control. US Treasury Secretary Scott Basnet confirmed new sanctions on a Turkish bank and its affiliates for facilitating IRGC Quds Force transactions and claimed the EU has joined the "economic expulsion" campaign. President Trump's envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, are scheduled to visit Moscow and Kyiv for talks on ending the Ukraine war. The US House of Representatives passed a bill sanctioning universities boycotting Israel. The Pentagon reportedly advised against using the term "Operation Epic Fury" for the Iran conflict, as it officially ended on May 5th, while acknowledging ongoing consequences.

**Gulf States**: Qatar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned Iranian actions as "clear violation of international law," asserting that Qatar is not a party to the conflict. Oman reportedly rejected Iran's proposal for shared fees for transit through the Strait of Hormuz. The UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed discussed regional developments with Turkish President Erdogan.

**European Union (EU) Members**: France's Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot stated that Paris did not choose the war against Iran but is bearing its economic costs and is preparing an international mission to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Germany is tightening security at power substations following suspected sabotage attacks, which its Interior Ministry described as not coincidental ahead of upcoming regional elections. The EU has reportedly supported the US economic campaign against Iran, with US Treasury Secretary Basnet claiming their official participation.

**Russia**: A Russian drone struck the SBU building in Kyiv, which Ukrainian President Zelenskyy confirmed, alleging it was an attempt to assassinate the SBU head.

**China**: Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf expressed Iran's welcome for China's idea of a new security architecture for the region, emphasizing regional self-determination. Judiciary Chief Eje'i met with China’s Supreme People’s Court President Zhang Jun to expand judicial cooperation, noting China's key role in a new global order. Russneft stated that China's oil reserves and cooperation with Moscow have shielded it from the Hormuz crisis.

**Turkey**: The US Treasury sanctioned a Turkish bank and two affiliates for ties to Iran. Turkish President Erdogan discussed regional developments with UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed. Reports from NAYA indicate Turkish intelligence will oversee the PKK's disarmament in Iraq.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions persist regarding Iranian military actions and their impact. While Iranian sources, including the Army Spokesperson, explicitly claimed missile and drone attacks on US bases in Jordan and the UAE, senior US officials denied knowledge of such attacks on their bases in Jordan. Al Arabiya, however, reported interceptions in northern Jordan, suggesting some form of projectiles were indeed in the air. This discrepancy requires further verification to ascertain the extent and effectiveness of any alleged Iranian strikes.

The figure of "767 US troops wounded in the war with Iran," reported solely by Press TV, lacks corroboration from any other source and should be treated as unverified propaganda. Similarly, the Iranian narrative of having successfully bypassed the US naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz contrasts sharply with US claims of effectively choking off Iran's oil exports and extracting 15 million barrels of oil.

Differing accounts of the Ali al-Taher ridge operation exist. While Israel declared full capture and destruction of Hezbollah's effective military capabilities, Press TV reports that Israeli forces "continue to target" the area, implying ongoing resistance rather than full control. The IRGC official's statement about 70-100 Hezbollah and IRGC Quds Force members trapped in tunnels adds a specific, unverified detail that underscores the high stakes of the operation.

Propaganda indicators include the framing of the conflict as a "war" or "US-Israeli aggression" by Iranian sources, contrasting with US officials who prefer not to use the term "war." The German Interior Ministry's assertion that power grid sabotages before elections are "no coincidence" hints at attributing responsibility without concrete evidence, potentially for political gain. The "purported claim of responsibility" for the German sabotage attacks, being handwritten and identifying the alleged sender, also raises questions about its authenticity and could be a disinformation attempt.

Reporting gaps include the precise status of the trapped Hezbollah/IRGC personnel in Ali al-Taher, the specific impact of alleged Iranian strikes on US bases, and detailed independent assessments of the economic impact of the Strait of Hormuz situation on Iran beyond US Treasury statements.
